summary: The note describes how local education systems since September 2023 are bringing parents and communities in as co-architects of education. It covers Educational Councils, the Ed-Connect app, community service learning, educator training grants, new assessment metrics, and Community Learning Fairs. It concludes that education is becoming a shared responsibility between schools, families, and communities.
one_line: Since September 2023, local education systems have expanded parent and community roles through councils, apps, service learning, training, new metrics, and learning fairs.
key_facts: Dr. Maria Stevenson is described as the leading voice in community-based educational reform; her book "The Community Classroom: Education Beyond Boundaries" was released on November 15, 2023.

Educational Councils bring together parents, business leaders, and other community stakeholders monthly to deliberate on curriculum design, resource allocation, and individualized student success strategies.
Meadowville Independent School District launched its first Educational Council on January 20, 2024, including Laura Jackson, a parent and local entrepreneur, alongside educators and students.
Westbridge's council began on February 5, 2024, and was instrumental in creating the 'Youth Innovation Hub,' which blends local industry experience with student learning objectives.
The 'Ed-Connect' app was piloted in Boulder Valley School District on September 3, 2023, letting parents interact with educators and join curriculum review sessions in real time.
Jennifer Lee, a tech developer and parent from Boulder Valley, said "Ed-Connect has democratized education."
The Ed-Connect pilot's success led to widescale adoption, with districts across the state integrating similar technology.

Service learning projects initiated after September 1, 2023 include urban farming in marginalized neighborhoods, technology literacy programs for the elderly, and environmental conservation initiatives.
Charlie Thompson, a student at Elmwood High School, said working on the Green Roof Project showed how school learning can transform communities.

Since October 10, 2023, professional development has focused on community engagement and cultural competency, and the State Department of Education announced grant programs for workshops and seminars.
Principal George Kildare of Springfield Elementary advocates such training, saying teachers shape "civic participants and future leaders."
Dr. Javier Ramon leads research on new assessment metrics, including the "Engagement Index," which looks at the impact of community integration on academic progress.
Evaluations now consider parental and community engagement rather than solely standardized test scores.

Community Learning Fairs, held since December 2023, showcase student projects developed with local businesses, non-profits, and civic groups; organizer Reginald Banks says they symbolize erasing the education/community divide.
